column2: Smearing one (portion) and putting the other in a cooking vessel, he should stir the purified rice grains in cow's milk and cook them.
Pure, with hair purified, chanting the mantra, he should cook the offering (charu); having removed the charu, it should be given in the fire by rule.
Having worshipped with incense, lamps and the like, the wise one should offer the charu soaked in ghee in a consecrated fire a hundred and eight times.
Thus the mantra-knower should offer on seven Fridays; quarrels in the field vanish, and troubles from enemies, thieves and the like.
On a Tuesday at sunrise he should again take clay from the field to be gained, prepare the offering as before,
and with respect offer in the kindled fire the same number as before. Thus on seven Tuesdays he should offer for success of the field.
He should offer a hundred thousand with cow products and milk-rice; he gets lordship over the land he desires, without doubt.
With a shining arm-bar lifted, the mountain-earth on his white tusk-tip, golden — in the yellow earth-circle, attentive,
meditating on Varaha, one gets a lovely earth by Varaha's grace. In the water-circle he should meditate on Varaha, bright as snow:
for the practitioner the great calamities are pacified, without doubt. For subduing, he should always meditate on one peacock-bright in the fire-circle;
for driving away enemies, one dark in the wind-circle; Varaha in the clear horse-circle gives all success.
For pacifying enemies, spirits, planets, fevers, diseases and afflictions: with the head adorned with a dot of space and joined with "bhagavat",
the one-syllable Varaha mantra is another wish-granting tree. Worship, arghya and all else should be done with it as stated before.
With the left ear (letter), "Varahaya" with the heart at the end, beginning with Om, eight-syllabled — it gives all lordship.
Brahma is the sage, Gayatri the metre, the deity is called Varaha; the limb-rite is conceived with (moon-sky-seas-eyes) syllables.
Meditation, worship and application should be done as before. At the start Om and the dative, then the word "Bhagavati", then "Dharani" twice, then "Hare" twice should be said.

clothed in variegated garments, the Lady Dhara. Having meditated thus, he should chant a hundred thousand and offer a tenth in milk-rice.

When the mantra is perfected, the practitioner accomplishes his own desire. Worshipping the Earth with animals, jewels, garments and the like,
he becomes the beloved of the Earth, lives happily a hundred years. The Trailokyamohana mantra of Jagannatha is told:
he becomes the beloved of the Earth, lives happily a hundred years. The Trailokyamohana mantra of Jagannatha is told:
Om, Kama, Rama (seeds), at the end of heart (hrid), Purushottama; Shrikantha at the end of "pratirupa"; "Lakshmi" and "nivasin" ...

Then at the end of "sakala" the word "jagat", then "kshobhana"; at the end of "sarvastrihridaya" he should say "vidarana";

then ending with "tribhuvana", "madonmadakara"; at the end of "surasura", the class of "manuja-sundari"...

Manamsi tapaya twice, "dipaya" twice, then "shoshaya" twice, then "maraya" twice,
stambhaya twice, "mohaya" twice, "dravaya" twice, then "akarshaya" twice,
stambhaya twice, "mohaya" twice, "dravaya" twice, then "akarshaya" twice,
joined with "samastaparama" and "subhaga"; at the end of "sarvasaubhagya", he should say "kara-sarva".
Kamapradaya, Brahma, moon, "hanu" twice, then "with the discus", "with the mace", then "with the sword",
with all arrows pierce twice, "with the noose" at the end "katadvaya", saying "with the goad", "strike" twice again,
kuru twice, then "kim tishthasi" (why do you stand?), until the end of the word, attentively afterward; "then grant me success", and at the end the armour "phat".
This great mantra, ending in the heart, is declared of two hundred syllables. Its sage is said to be Jaimini; the metre is declared limitless;
the deity is called Jagannatha, in bewildering the worlds. Kama is the seed, Rama is the power; the application is for gaining all.
Purushottama-tribhuvana-unmadaka and fire-armour, then the heart is declared with the word "jagatkshobhana";
the head is called "Lakshmi-dayita" ending in armour; the tuft again; "Manmatha", at the end "tama", he should say in "manmathe";
saying "Kamadaya hum" he should place the armour, then after "parama" with "Bhrigu" and "karna", the word "sarva",
at the end of "saubhagyakara" with armour, the shield is declared. At the end of "surasura" he should say "manuja-sundari",
at the end of heart, then "vida", then "rana-sarva"; then "praharanadhara-sarvakamuka",
hana twice and the heart; then "bandhanani"; "akarshaya" twice, then "mahabala",
armour and weapon declared, then the eye; he should say "tribhuvana", then "chara sarvajana",
manamsi hara twice, "daraya" twice for me; "vasham anaya" with armour at the end — the eye mantra is declared.
The six limb mantras, beginning with Om, ending in "phat" and "namah", are declared. Om, at the end of "trailokya", the word "mohana",
after saying "Hrishikesha" and from the word "apratirupa", after "manmatha" he should say "sarvastrinam hridayam",
akarshana, "gaccha agaccha" ending in the heart. By this, having made it all-pervading, the wise one should remember Jagannatha.
On the bank of the Milk Ocean, lovely, adorned with creepers of wish-trees, bright as a mass of rising suns, shining by its own radiance in all directions,
with the fragrance of rows of flowers, the humming of intoxicated bees, with garments dusted by pollen of lotuses moving in the divine breeze,
a charming forest with the sweetness of songs of celestial women: he should contemplate it. Within it a pavilion with arches shining with gem wealth,
with a canopy with garlands of pearls shining, with a gem-dais and so on, worshipped with the crown tips in the sky,
seated on a divine lion-throne, O Brahmin, he should remember the Lord, holding in his arms conch, noose, bows, pestle, Nandaka sword, mace,
goad, embraced on the lotus-chest, looking at Lakshmi seated on his lap with eyes sparkling with love.
Having meditated thus, he should chant four hundred thousand and offer a tenth part in a semicircular fire-pit with lotuses or jasmine flowers.
Intending to worship Jagannatha, the wise one should sprinkle the sacrificial ground, himself and the ritual implements with the Gayatri:
Trailokyamohanaya, at the end he should say "vidmahe"; "Smaraya dhimahi", then "Tan no Vishnuh prachodayat".
This is declared the Gayatri, the supreme purifier of all. The wise one should place a seat on the Vaishnava pitha described before.
Pakshirajaya with two "tha": this is declared the seat mantra. Conceiving the form with the root mantra, he should invoke it there.
Then, with the all-pervading placing mantra, worshipping with devotion, by it he should worship Shrivatsa on the breasts as the heart-Shrivatsa;
with "Kaustubhaya" ending in the heart, the Kaustubha on the chest; the forest garland with the heart-ending on the neck.
Then he should worship the deities of the limbs on the pericarp by rule; then on the petals the Lakshmi and others waving chowries,
bright as bandhuka flowers, their breasts shining with pearl necklaces, lotus-eyed, slow with the play of intoxication.
Lakshmi, Sarasvati, Dhriti, Priti, then Kanti, Shanti, Tushti, Pushti — with the seeds in the dative.
The seed of the goddess is declared: "Bhrigu" with "kha", "ra", "sa" and moon; with the three short vowels and without the neuter...
the seed of the goddess is to be applied first, in order, to them. On the petal tips he should worship the conch, Sharnga bow, discus, sword, mace,
goad, pestle, noose, each with its own mudra and mantras. "Mahajalachara" at the end, armour, weapon and "svaha".
Panchajanya for the worship of the conch, with Om at the beginning and "namah" at the end; for the Sharnga, with armour, weapon and "svaha",
Sharngaya hridayam is the mantra in the worship of Sharnga, beginning with "maha". At the end of "Sudarshana-maha", he should say "chakraraja",
haya twice, "sarvadushtabhaya", at the end "kuru" twice, "chhindhi" twice, then "vidaraya" twice,
paramantran grasa twice, "bhakshaya" twice, "bhutani trasaya" twice, armour, "phat", "svaha".
Sudarshanaya hridayam is the mantra in the worship of the discus. After "mahakhadga-tikshna" he should say "chhindhi" twice,
hum phat svaha, "Khadgaya namah" is the mantra in sword-worship. After "Mahakaumodaki" he should say "mahabale",
sarvasurantake, then "prasida" twice; armour, weapon, "svaha"; "Kaumodakyai hrit".
In the worship of Kaumodaki, the mantra is declared as accomplishing all aims. After "mahankusha", "kuta" twice, "hum phat svaha":
Ankushaya namah is the mantra in goad-worship. After "Samvartaka-maha" he should say "musala",
yodhaya twice, armour, "phat" at the end, "svaha"; "Musalaya namah" is the mantra in pestle-worship.
Mahapasha ... ghataya akarshaya twice, "hum phat svaha"; "Pashaya namah" is the mantra in noose-worship.
These mantras begin with Om. Then he should worship Indra and the rest.
Having worshipped Vajra and the rest, he becomes lord of all success. For a month, worshipping with flowers born of "hayari" (kind of oleander),
or offering with lilies a thousand and eight, within a month all the best kings become subject to him.
He who chants the mantra joined with a person's name ten thousand times becomes his servant at once, by the power of this mantra.
What more need be said here? With this mantra the practitioner accomplishes all desires and becomes equal to Vishnu, without doubt.
He should chant the mantra a hundred thousand and offer a tenth part with milk-rice, mixed with ghee, in the fire; he should worship on the seat stated before.
Having first worshipped the limbs, he should worship Garuda and others on the petals in the directions, Shrimukha and others in the corners, and the world-guardians outside.
A mantra so accomplished fulfils all desires. In a gentle task he should remember the gentle (form), in a cruel one the cruel.
Having first spoken the enemy's name in the place of death, he should himself remember Hari devouring him with sharp claws and tusk-tips.
Chanting daily a hundred and eight times unwearied, within a hundred days the enemy becomes a guest of Yama.
Now I shall tell the varieties of meditation, giving all success. One desiring prosperity should constantly meditate on the white Nrihari as before,
embraced by Lakshmi seated on his left lap, with a lotus in her hand, destroying poison, untimely death, diseases and all calamities.
Narasimha, most terrible, bright as the fire of the end of time, wearing a garland of entrails, fierce, adorned with a necklace,
with a serpent as sacred thread, resplendent with five faces, moon-crested, blue-throated, three-eyed on each face,
adorned with ten arms like iron bars, holding rosary, mace, lotus, conch bright as cow's milk,
bow, pestle and the excellent discus, sword, trident and arrow — Nrihari in Rudra's form;
the colours of Indra-gopa insect, blue, moon, gold: from the east to the north and upward, all colours.
Having meditated thus, the practitioner should chant for release from all disease; remembering this divine form destroys all death and grants all success.
When one meditates for a great task, then Narasimha, lord of all worlds, adorned with all ornaments, should be sixteen-armed.
Two arms engaged in tearing, two drawing out entrails, two holding conch and discus, two bow and arrow,
two sword and shield, two mace and lotus, two noose and goad, two set upon the enemy's crown —
such Nrihari, adorned with sixteen arms: O Narada, with undistracted mind one should meditate on him, blue, of fierce deeds.
In the greatest task the wise should meditate on Narasimha, lord of all beings, giver of all success, the supreme, thirty-two-armed.
On the right: discus and lotus, axe and noose, plough and pestle, protection and goad,
pattisha, bhindipala, sword, mudgara, tomara; on the left side in the hands: conch, shield, noose, trident,
fire, boon, spear, water-pot, then bow, the finger-pointing gesture, mace, drum and winnowing basket;
with two hands pressing the enemy's knee and head; with two hands raised wearing the garland of entrails;
with two hands below tearing Hiranyakashipu, dear to devotees and frightening to demons —
one should remember Narasimha thus, who removes the fear of great death. Having meditated thus, the practitioner should chant for success of all aims.
Now another meditation is told, auspicious, removing diseases of the mouth: seated on golden Garuda, with a garland of lightning-bright mane,
moon-coloured like ten million full moons, fair-faced, three-eyed, adorned with yellow cloth and thighs, Narasimha of peaceful form, holding discus, conch, protection and boon in his lotus-hands:
it quells diseases like poison; made happy by his own meditations. By stopping the enemy's army, the practitioner should make effort.
In a fire kindled with akshaka wood, contemplating the crushing of the enemy, having worshipped the god Narasimha with flowers and other offerings,
he should offer one thousand with roots and charu each separately; chanting as if devouring the enemy, as if burning him he should throw him.
Having offered for seven days, the mantra-knower should dispatch the king's chosen army at an auspicious ascendant, wishing to conquer the enemy's land.
Remembering Nrihari destroying the enemy host before it, he should continue the chant until it returns.
Having conquered all enemies with heroic prosperity, happily, the king, pleased in mind, should satisfy the mantra-knower with wealth,
with elephants, horses, chariots, jewels, villages, fields, wealth and the like. If the mantra-knower is not satisfied, then calamity befalls the king:
in his realms there arises great fear even for life. Ash consecrated by chanting the root mantra a hundred and eight times
destroys poison arisen from mice, spiders, scorpions and so on; smeared on the body one is freed from all diseases, without doubt.
Offering with sevanti flowers he would gain great prosperity; with udumbara fuel-sticks he becomes rich in grain;
offering a hundred thousand cakes he becomes like Kubera. Before an angry king he should chant a hundred and eight times;
at once he gains cleanness and attains favour. With jasmine flowers, prosperity; with plantain, the removal of obstacles.
By offering tulsi leaves he gains great fame; by offering barley-flour from rice he subdues the whole world;
with madhuka flowers desire is gained; with pieces of amalaka, paralysis (of enemies). Guduchi four finger-breadths long, mixed with curd, honey and ghee,
he who offers ten thousand lives a hundred years and conquers disease. On a Saturday, touching the ashvattha and chanting a hundred and eight times,
he conquers untimely death and lives a hundred years. Now I shall tell you the Trailokyamohana yantra,
by merely wearing which all prosperity comes: on white birch-bark he should draw a lotus with thirty-two lions,
in the middle lion his own seed, written as before; with the Shri seed surrounding it, with three rings,
enclosed with noose and goad: he should worship the best yantra named Trailokyamohana, accomplisher of all desired aims.
The king of wheels, the great king, lord of lords of all wheels: by wearing it one gains victory, true, true, without doubt.
Now I shall tell another yantra, Narada, giving success; hear. He should draw an eight-spoked yantra, smooth, with a pericarp;
he should write the root mantra there with Om, the one-syllable Narasimha, and in the middle with the object of the rite;
chant eight thousand, wrapping it with thread outside, and the wise one should wrap it in order with gold, silver and copper;
having wrapped it with lac, he should again consecrate it with the mantra; he should wear the best yantra on the neck, arm or tuft.
Men, women and kings on earth all become subject to him; wicked ghouls, serpents and demons do not trouble him.
By the grace of the king of yantras he gains victory everywhere. Now I shall tell another yantra that subdues all:
the wise one should draw a twelve-spoked great wheel as before, with petals divided by the twelve vowel-measures.
